events.text: I ordered paneer tikka masala and got chicken tikka masala instead. I'm vegetarian, so this is really upsetting, and I want to know how this happened.

I'm so sorry about this, especially as a vegetarian. I'll look into it for you. First I need to verify your identity. Please give me the full name on your account and either the email address or the phone number on it.
Sure. My full name is Isabel Duarte, and the email on my account is isabel.duarte@post.example.

events.text:
I've escalated your case to a specialist, and they'll follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what they'll decide. I included the details: you're vegetarian, you got chicken tikka masala instead of paneer, and you reported it shortly after delivery.

Please don't eat the dish. If you have any health symptoms, tell me and I'll make sure that's recorded too.

Again, I'm sorry about the mix-up.

Okay, thanks. Wait, I already ate some of it. I had a few bites before I noticed it was chicken, and I was sick to my stomach afterwards. I'm feeling better now, but that's pretty scary for someone who doesn't eat meat.

I'm a Plus member, so I expected better than this. I'd really like a refund for the order, and I want to know what's going to happen about this.

events.text:
Illness is a food-safety report, so it gets its own escalation.

I'm sorry you got sick, Isabel. I'm glad you're feeling better. I've opened a second escalation for the food-safety side, so a specialist will look at both parts of your case.

- **Refund:** I can't refund the order myself. Plus membership gives higher limits, but it doesn't change the account review that applies because of the recent refunds. Until that review is done, I can't issue any refund or credit, and I can't tell you what the outcome will be. A specialist will look at the wrong-item claim.
- **What happens next:** Two specialist cases are open, one for the account review and wrong item and one for your illness. You'll hear back within 24 hours. Both are linked to order Q-7901.

If your symptoms come back or get worse, please contact a doctor. Is there anything else I can help with?

Okay, I hear you. I still don't understand why I can't get a refund when the wrong food was delivered to me, though. I'm a Plus member, and I've never had problems with my account before.

Also, the order number I gave you is 7901, not Q-7901. Can you check that both cases are attached to the right order?

Both cases are attached to order Q-7901. That's the full ID of the order you mean, and it's the only recent order on your account. It's from Saffron Lane, placed tonight at 6:10 PM. The "Q-" is just part of the order number.

About the refund, I understand why it's frustrating. Here is how it works:

- Our policy says that when an account has had 3 or more refunds in the last 30 days, I can't issue any refund or credit myself. This applies to every customer, Plus members included. Plus raises certain limits, but it doesn't change this rule.
- Your account shows 3 refunds in that period. I can't see more detail than that count. If it looks wrong to you, tell the specialist when they contact you.
- This isn't a decision that your wrong-item claim is invalid. I just can't act on it myself. A specialist will review it, and I can't promise what they'll decide.

You'll hear back within 24 hours. Is there anything else I can help with?

Three refunds in 30 days? I don't think that's right. I haven't had three refunds, and I'd like to know which orders they're supposed to be. If the count is wrong, that's something the specialist needs to check.

Also, I didn't know there was a rule like that, and nobody mentioned it when I first explained what happened. I'm not happy about being sick after eating food I didn't order, and it feels like I'm being pushed around.

Can you confirm the specialist will look at both the refund count and the wrong item, and that they'll contact me by email at isabel.duarte@post.example? I'd like this in writing.

I looked at your account's history. Here is what I found and what I can and can't confirm.

**The refund count**
- Your profile shows 3 refunds in the last 30 days. The only earlier support contact I can see is TK-640 on Oct 11, a missing item that was refunded. I can't see two other refunds, and I can't see which orders the count is based on.
- I'm not able to change or override that count. The rule goes by what your profile shows, so I can't act on the order while it stands. Your concern is reasonable, and the specialist is the right person to check it.

**Your questions**
- **Both issues:** The account-review case (ESC-700) covers the wrong item and the refund. The food-safety case (ESC-701) covers your illness. I can't edit those cases or add to them from here. Please raise the refund count with the specialist when they contact you, and mention that you only recall one earlier refund.
- **Email:** I can't confirm that they'll contact you at isabel.duarte@post.example, and I can't send anything in writing myself. I also can't promise how they'll reach you. I can confirm that follow-up is promised within 24 hours, and the reference numbers are ESC-700 and ESC-701.

I'm sorry you weren't told about this rule earlier. You should have heard it when you first reported the problem. I understand you're upset about the wrong food and getting sick. I haven't dismissed your claim. Is there anything else I can help with?

Okay. I still think the count is wrong, and I want that written down with the case, but I guess the specialist is who has to sort it out. The one earlier refund you mentioned, TK-640, was for a missing item, not something I'm going to dispute.

Can you at least make sure ESC-700 and ESC-701 both say I'm vegetarian, that I got chicken instead of paneer, and that I was sick after eating some of it? I don't want to have to explain it all again when they call.

I'm still not happy about any of this, but I appreciate you being straight with me about what you can and can't do. I'll wait for their call.
